clue.text: Study the translation for a change

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a version is a rendering of a text in another language

explanation.surface: A student swaps one language for another and finds the exercise a welcome change.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversion is a transformation from one form, belief or use to another.

clue.text: Scolded, many concealed themselves

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
hid is the past tense of hide, to conceal oneself

explanation.surface: After a telling-off, a crowd of people went into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: CHID is an old past tense of chide, to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To chide is to rebuke, and the archaic past form matches the past participle scolded.

clue.text: Like a flight of bees, very matey

definitions.meaning: a queen bee's mating flight is called her ... flight
a pun: matey read as to do with mating, i.e. pertaining to marriage

explanation.surface: Bees swarming together look extremely friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to marriage or mating, as in the bees' wedding flight.

clue.text: Banbury 'Cross's fine lady. for instance

parts.note: the nursery rhyme Ride a cock-horse to Banbury Cross has a fine lady upon a white horse, a female rider

explanation.surface: A nod to the nursery rhyme heroine of Banbury Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: Banbury Cross is in Oxfordshire; the English nursery rhyme sends the child to see a fine lady riding a white horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's lady sits upon a white horse, making her a horsewoman, a female rider.

clue.text: Bones of poet found outside Egypt's capital

indicators.note: the poet's name is found wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: John Skelton was a Tudor poet, tutor to Henry VIII

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the word Egypt's is taken

explanation.surface: A poet's remains are discovered somewhere beyond Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egypt's capital' looks like Cairo but gives only its first letter E, which goes inside SKELTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the framework of bones of a body.

clue.text: Monocotyledonous alternative to 1 dn

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: a plant whose seedlings have a single seed leaf

parts.note: or is the word that introduces an alternative
the answer to 1 down, a word meaning scolded

explanation.surface: A botanist offers a single-seed-leaf plant as a substitute for another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective standing in for the plant it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchids are a large family of flowering plants classed among the monocots, with one seed leaf.

clue.text: A supporter of the theatre?

parts.note: reads like a patron of the arts, but means a stage ..., also a word for a physical support

explanation.surface: Who is a loyal patron of the stage?
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is both a support holding something up and an object used on stage by actors.

clue.text: Performance of citizen in adaptation of " Lear "

indicators.note: the citizen is placed in the middle of the rearranged play title
an adaptation reworks the play's name, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: cit is a short, old word for a citizen or townsman

explanation.surface: An ordinary townsman stars in a new stage version of Shakespeare's King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptation of' rearranges LEAR into REAL, and 'in' puts CIT into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetic performance given by one or a few performers.

clue.text: Outlaws in favour of writers

parts.note: pro is Latin-derived for for, in favour of
scribes are people who write documents by hand

explanation.surface: Bandits sympathise with authors.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or banish, the verb outlaws used in the same sense.

clue.text: Indiscretion might, right away, amount to cheek

indicators.note: the clue says the answer with right taken away comes to cheek, so right sits inside the cheeky word

parts.note: cheek is impertinence or insolence

explanation.surface: A careless remark might, quite rightly, be seen as sheer insolence.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take R ('right away') out of the answer and it 'amounts to' IMPUDENCE, cheek; so R goes into IMPUDENCE. 'might' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is lack of caution or good judgement, which is what an indiscretion shows.

clue.text: Narcissus's loving imitator

parts.note: in Greek myth a nymph doomed only to repeat others' words fell in love with Narcissus

explanation.surface: A devoted mimic of a vain young man.
explanation.definitionFit: The nymph of Ovid's tale could only repeat the last words she heard, pining for the youth who loved his reflection.

clue.text: The time a harp disfigured a scene of contest

indicators.note: something disfigured has lost its shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Long ago a harp was damaged during a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is an open arena, like the Colosseum, where gladiatorial contests were staged.

clue.text: Inclination to purchase for ourselves, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: buy us means purchase on our behalf

explanation.surface: We feel an urge to treat ourselves to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A bias is a leaning or tendency towards one side.

clue.text: So puzzling. Nimrod's notes

definitions.meaning: Nimrod is a movement of Elgar's Enigma Variations, so its notes come from the Enigma

explanation.surface: A mysterious set of notes left by a mighty hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: Nimrod is the biblical hunter, but here is the famous ninth of Elgar's Enigma Variations.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means mysterious or puzzling, and Nimrod's music belongs to the Enigma set.

clue.text: Unkempt beard on a Scotsman — Angus perhaps ?

indicators.note: unkempt hair is messed up, so these letters are tousled

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot with a scruffy beard, possibly called Angus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unkempt' rearranges BEARDON into ABERDON, and IAN follows; 'a' is a link. Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland, and Angus a common Scots name.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdonian is a native of Aberdeen, and Angus is a typical name for such a Scotsman.

clue.text: Dancing place for everyone in the plant

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes inside the plant

parts.note: broom is a yellow-flowered shrub
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A dance floor is set up for the whole crowd among the shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large hall used for formal dancing.

clue.text: S. American republic is said to produce this relish?

indicators.note: is said means the country's name is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Chile is a republic on the west coast of South America

explanation.surface: A South American country claims to make a certain sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli is a hot pepper or a spicy seasoning, a relish in the old sense of a sharp flavour.

clue.text: Leaning to port?.Then choose from this

indicators.note: to means attached to, so the second piece is joined on

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a ship's list is a lean to one side

explanation.surface: A ship tilting to its left side, then a diner picking a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests a ship's left side alongside the list, but here it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine list is the menu of wines in a restaurant, from which diners pick.

clue.text: Uproar associated with court proceedings

definitions.meaning: a bat strung for tennis or squash, games played on a court

explanation.surface: Noisy scenes break out during a legal trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a din, and also the strung bat used in court games like tennis.

clue.text: A number of bids for the boxes

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
bids are offers, as at an auction

explanation.surface: Several tenders are made for some boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes for keeping money or valuables.

clue.text: Tricky test said to cause repugnance

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward or devious, so these letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A difficult exam reportedly provokes disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is dislike or aversion, close to revulsion.

clue.text: Therefore the art chief has no voice

parts.note: so means therefore
PRA is the President of the Royal Academy, head of London's art academy

explanation.surface: Thus the head of the art world loses the power of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy of Arts is a London art institution; its president signs PRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is the highest singing voice, or a singer with it.

clue.text: A chirpy creature, the bounder in American intelligence

indicators.note: the cad sits inside the intelligence agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is an ill-mannered man, an old-fashioned bounder

explanation.surface: A cheeky fellow working as a US spy.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is an insect famous for its loud chirping song.

clue.text: Disgusting attack

explanation.definitionFit: Offensive means repellent as an adjective and an assault as a noun.

clue.text: Observe some Guy Fawkes pyrotechnics

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, running across them

explanation.surface: Watch the fireworks on Guy Fawkes Night.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes Night, 5 November, is celebrated in Britain with bonfires and fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or notice.

clue.text: Farm building. constructed by engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: A barn put up by army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed.

clue.text: In the same place formerly as a mountain goat

parts.note: ib is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place, used in footnotes
ex means former, as in an ex-wife

explanation.surface: A goat found back where it used to be.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat of the Alps with long curved horns.

clue.text: Fine decisions may be made by this body

definitions.text: Fine decisions may be made by this body

parts.words: Fine decisions may be made by this body
parts.note: fine reads as excellent, but means a monetary penalty imposed by a court of justices

explanation.surface: A wise committee is good at making decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: British magistrates' courts handle minor offences, often punishing them with fines.
explanation.definitionFit: The magistracy is the body of magistrates, who impose penalties such as fines.

clue.text: Uncle Arly's cricket supporter

parts.note: in Edward Lear's poem about Uncle Arly, a cricket perched on part of his face

explanation.surface: An uncle who cheers on a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket suggests the British bat-and-ball game, but in Lear's poem it is the insect, sitting on his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear wrote that on Uncle Arly's beak a cricket sat, so that facial feature supported it.

clue.text: Washing implement for striking games players?

definitions.meaning: a wooden paddle once used to beat laundry
the bat used in the old game with a shuttlecock, struck between players

explanation.surface: A laundry tool used for hitting sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore was a paddle for beating washing and also the racket of battledore and shuttlecock.
